findings_to_judge.claim: Cango has published no monthly operational / bitcoin-production update since 2026-06-10 (May data): its own newsroom shows nothing between the 2026-06-24 EGM result and the 2026-08-25 earnings-date notice, so June, July and August updates are all missing -- an 82-day gap against a monthly cadence the company had held since at least mid-2025, and while peer Canaan kept publishing (June update on 2026-07-14). The market's last hashrate/production/treasury data point is therefore 31.67 EH/s, 237.59 BTC and 1,065.11 BTC as of 2026-05-31, and tonight's release supplies the June number nobody has.

Cango's own April 2026 release disclosed an average cash cost of $68,061 per coin, while BTC traded around $62,953-$63,400 through June 2026 -- so Cango self-mined at a negative cash margin for most of the quarter being reported, on a cash balance of $7.2m at 31 March (down from $41.2m at year-end) and with Q2 self-mined production of only 466.5 BTC in April+May against 1,266.1 BTC in the whole of Q1.

The AI pivot that carries the equity story is, on inspection of the company's own live product site, a small self-serve GPU cloud: ecohash.com sells single-to-8-GPU instances of NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 (96GB Blackwell) workstation cards, LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning on 1-4 GPUs, an OpenAI-compatible inference API from $0.02/1M tokens, and a $1 free credit on signup, with no customer logos or case studies. Management guided on the Q1 call only that 'revenue generation will start in the second half of this year' with no targets.

Today's close is the mechanical NYSE compliance test and it passes. The 2026-03-10 NYSE deficiency notice gave a six-month cure period expiring around 2026-09-10, curable only 'on the last trading day of any calendar month during the Cure Period' with both a $1.00 close and a $1.00 average close over the trailing 30 trading days. 31 August is the last month-end inside that window, and it is exactly the 30th trading day since the 10-for-1 consolidation took effect on 21 July (9 July sessions + 21 August sessions, no intervening holiday) -- so this is the first and last month-end on which the whole lookback is post-consolidation tape. At $2.27-2.41 today and a 52-week low of $1.36, both prongs clear.

Antalpha's Q2 2026 report -- filed 2026-08-19, i.e. after Cango last spoke and reporting on the same 30 June balance-sheet date -- states that revenue excluding 'the Cango facility repaid in the first quarter of 2026' was $11.6m, that technology financing fees fell 40% y/y 'primarily reflecting the wind-down of the Cango facility', and that Antalpha has recorded no principal loss since inception. That is the counterparty confirming, from the other side of the ledger, that Cango's bitcoin-collateralised borrowing is fully extinguished with no credit event -- which implies the $68.2m of 'Bitcoin collateral receivables' on Cango's 31 March balance sheet releases into unencumbered BTC during Q2.
